title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets
read_level: full (v3, dated 20 Nov 2026 on the PDF; first-version date taken from metadata)
metadata_mismatch: Metadata author "Eduardo C. Garrido-Merchán" (hyphenated); paper byline "Eduardo C. Garrido Merchán". Read version is v3.
why_wsp: An LLM (Claude Opus 5, plus Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5, Grok 4.7) reads a full small tabular dataset in context and writes every weight and bias of a linear or 8-unit ReLU MLP as literal numbers, with no code execution and no evaluation of the network before sealing.
domain: tabular supervised learning (toy, rotated synthetic, Iris/Wine/Breast Cancer, concrete compressive strength regression)
editor: Claude Opus 5 (xhigh effort) main; Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Grok 4.7 comparison arms; open-weight series Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B, Qwen3 4B, Ministral 8B (4-bit)
target: linear map and mlp8 (one hidden layer of 8 ReLU units) per rung; small (tens to ~100 parameters)

headline_results.quote: the hand-written network reaches a coefficient of determination of 0.9997 against 0.9997 for least squares

headline_results.claim: Parity rung solved exactly, above all baselines
headline_results.quote: The result classifies all one hundred and twenty held-out rows correctly, above the Bayes rate of 0.9877
It scored 0.9460 against an irreducible ceiling of 0.9500, beating the best baseline at 0.9312.
the construction nonetheless reached 0.5084 against 0.8594 for the trained network of the same shape
On s5_spiral the construction scored 0.5750, which is below its own linear arm at 0.6167
The construction scores 0.7444 against 0.7892 for the same architecture trained by gradient descent, 0.8749 for gradient-boosted trees
On r2_kink Grok reaches 0.8448 against Opus's 0.5084, a difference that survives the Holm correction

headline_results.claim: Open-weight models up to 8B fail easiest rung
headline_results.quote: No arm reached a second rung. All five stopped on toy_line
Of the nineteen that declare a numeric interval, nine landed inside it.

cost.claim: Sonnet non-delivery consumed half a million output tokens per rung
cost.quote: with no module text emitted at any point, for half a million output tokens per rung at the higher of the two settings

baselines_and_controls: same architectures trained by Adam over 20 seeds (raw and standardised inputs), OLS / penalised logistic regression, LDA, QDA, nearest neighbour, random forest, gradient-boosted trees; irreducible error / Bayes rate; best half-plane by exhaustive search; hidden rotation/scaling/label permutation as contamination control; four constructor arms; open-weight size series
runs_and_variance: one pass per rung and architecture (deterministic constructions), one partition per rung; Wilson intervals, exact McNemar, paired bootstrap, Holm correction. Quote: "the binomial noise on a classification score of a hundred and twenty held-out rows is about four and a half points at ninety-five per cent confidence" (Sec 6)
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no distribution shift, fine-tuning or quantization tests of written networks)
verification: SHA-256 sealing of constructions before evaluation; AST validator forbidding imports/calls/loops; pre-registered score predictions; coordinate-wise comparison to closed-form optima; equivalence of linear and mlp8 checked to 1e-13; boundary verified by bisection along 1,000 rays
memorization_vs_reasoning: Synthetic tier with hidden Haar rotation, scaling and label permutation designed as load-bearing evidence against recall; classical datasets flagged as possibly memorised (cites Bordt et al. 2024). Caveat: "The synthetic rungs were generated by the same model that wrote the constructions, which knows the qualitative family of each one".
limitations_stated: One partition per rung; deterministic single-pass constructions; one main constructor model; four arms not a scaling curve; arms differ in isolation and delivery conditions; synthetic data generated by the constructing model; single real dataset; gap between 8B open-weight and frontier unsampled.
code_or_data: none found (paper states digests and pre-registration are released; no URL found in text)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming
Garrido Merchán 2026, Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games (manuscript)
notes_for_survey: Moves B2 writing from rule compilation to statistical inference from data in context, with sealing and pre-registration discipline. Provides a formal definition of 'weight-space programmed' and separates non-delivery, confident-but-bad delivery, and inadmissible output as distinct failure modes across constructors.
